# Analyzers

Registered in `legacy_audit/analyzers/__init__.py`, in this order (every analyzer whose `supports(file)` is true runs on a file; their results are cached per file under the analyzer's `name` and keyed by its `version`). The contract is in `legacy_audit/analyzers/base.py`; how to add one is in [../extending.md](../extending.md#add-an-analyzer).

| # | Name | Version | Class | Module | What it reads |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `build` | 1 | `BuildAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.build` | Build files: Maven, Gradle (best effort), Ant/Ivy and Makefiles. |
| 2 | `deps` | 2 | `DepsAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.deps` | Undeclared dependencies: jars/wars/ears (manifest, pom.properties, file name), npm ``package.json`` (with the Node.js version it asks for), npm lock files (``package-lock.json``, ``npm-shrinkwrap.json``, ``yarn.lock``, ``pnpm-lock.yaml``: the exact version of every package, direct or not), Bower ``bower.json`` and bundled JavaScript libraries. |
| 3 | `config` | 2 | `ConfigAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.config` | Configuration files (properties, XML, YAML, INI, JSON): JDBC URLs, hosts and URLs, queue names and CFT partners as integrations; credentials are reported masked, never copied. |
| 4 | `java` | 6 | `JavaAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.java` | Java sources (tree-sitter-java): classes, methods, annotations, imports, entry points, SQL in strings (JDBC, JdbcTemplate, Hibernate/JPA, Spring Data), endpoints (HTTP/SOAP, sockets, FTP, MQ/JMS) and services exposed by annotations (Spring MVC, JAX-WS, JAX-RS, EJB, Struts 2). |
| 5 | `web` | 3 | `WebAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.web` | Java web tier: Struts 1/2 configuration, ``web.xml``, Tiles, JSF ``faces-config.xml`` and pages (JSP, JSF facelets, HTML, Velocity, FreeMarker). |
| 6 | `typescript` | 2 | `TypeScriptAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.typescript` | TypeScript and JavaScript (tree-sitter-typescript): Angular, AngularJS and Node.js code. |
| 7 | `dotnet` | 1 | `DotnetAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.dotnet` | Microsoft .NET and Windows desktop files that are not code: project files, NuGet package lists, configuration, window layouts and ASP.NET pages (decision 134). |
| 8 | `basic` | 2 | `BasicAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.basic` | Visual Basic 6 and VB.NET, read line by line (no parser: decision 135). |
| 9 | `csharp` | 2 | `CSharpAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.csharp` | C# (tree-sitter-c-sharp): Windows Forms, WPF, ASP.NET, WCF, Windows services and data access (decision 136). |
| 10 | `spring` | 3 | `SpringAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.spring` | Spring XML configuration and XML-mapped data access. |
| 11 | `sql` | 1 | `SqlAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.sql` | SQL scripts, PL/SQL packages and DDL (``.sql``, ``.pks``/``.pkb``..., DDL exports in ``audit-inputs/ddl``). DML becomes ``SqlStatement``s; tables, views, sequences and PL/SQL units become ``DbObject``s. DML inside PL/SQL bodies is extracted too (source ``plsql``). |
| 12 | `shell` | 1 | `ShellAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.shell` | Scripts (sh/ksh/bash, Windows batch, Perl, Python) and crontab files. |
| 13 | `c_cpp` | 4 | `CAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.c_cpp` | C and C++ sources (tree-sitter-c / tree-sitter-cpp): functions, ``main()`` (a ``c-executable`` service named after the file), includes, called functions, ``system()``/``exec*``/``popen`` commands, file I/O, sockets, IBM MQ MQI calls and SQL (database client API calls and SQL text built in buffers, see :mod:`legacy_audit.analyzers.c_sql`). |
| 14 | `proc` | 3 | `ProcAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.proc` | Pro*C (``.pc``): the ``EXEC SQL`` blocks are blanked and the C is handed to the C analyzer, then the blocks become ``SqlStatement``s (source ``embedded``); ``PREPARE ... FROM :buffer`` is rebuilt from the C that fills the buffer. Pro*COBOL is handled by the COBOL analyzer, which reads ``EXEC SQL ... END-EXEC`` itself. |
| 15 | `cobol` | 4 | `CobolAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.cobol` | COBOL and Pro*COBOL (fixed or free format), copybooks and CICS BMS maps. |
| 16 | `jcl` | 1 | `JclAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.jcl` | z/OS JCL: jobs, steps, ``EXEC PGM=`` / procedure calls, DD datasets, in-stream procedures and DB2 ``RUN PROGRAM(...)`` under ``IKJEFT01``. A job is a ``BatchJob`` (scheduler ``jcl``); a catalogued procedure (``//NAME PROC``) is a ``jcl-proc`` symbol its callers link to. |
| 17 | `autosys` | 2 | `AutosysAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.autosys` | Autosys JIL (``audit-inputs/autosys/`` and any ``.jil``): ``insert_job`` / ``update_job`` / ``delete_job`` with ``job_type``, ``box_name``, ``command``, ``machine``, ``condition``, ``start_times``, ``days_of_week``, ``run_calendar``, ``date_conditions`` and ``watch_file``. |
| 18 | `mq` | 2 | `MqAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.mq` | IBM MQ MQSC exports (``audit-inputs/mq/``, ``*.mqsc``): ``DEFINE QLOCAL/QREMOTE/QALIAS/ QMODEL`` become ``MQ`` integrations (one per queue, merged with the producers and consumers the code analyzers find; transmission queues are skipped), ``DEFINE CHANNEL`` becomes an ``MQ-CHANNEL`` integration whose direction follows the channel type. Each carries the queue manager of the export (``qmgr``: nam... |
| 19 | `cft` | 2 | `CftAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.cft` | Axway CFT: configuration exports (``CFTPART``, ``CFTTCP``, ``CFTSEND``, ``CFTRECV``) and ``CFTUTIL SEND/RECV`` calls (the shell analyzer calls :func:`cftutil_integration`). |
| 20 | `servers` | 2 | `ServersAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.servers` | Application servers and web servers: which ones the application is built for or runs on. |
| 21 | `webservices` | 1 | `WebServicesAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.websvc` | Web services (REST and SOAP): the shared builders analyzers use, and the analyzer for the XML files that describe or deploy web services. |
| 22 | `metrics` | 3 | `MetricsAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.metrics` | The ``metrics`` analyzer: code units with cyclomatic complexity, and duplication windows. |
| 23 | `patterns` | 1 | `PatternsAnalyzer` | `legacy_audit.analyzers.patterns` | The ``patterns`` analyzer: runs the text rules of the enabled rule packs over one file. |

## Shared helper modules (not analyzers)

| Module | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `legacy_audit.analyzers.base` | Common analyzer interface. |
| `legacy_audit.analyzers.c_sql` | SQL text that C code builds in buffers, and SQL handed to database client APIs. |
| `legacy_audit.analyzers.cobol_sql` | SQL text that COBOL builds in working storage for ``PREPARE ... FROM :var`` and ``EXECUTE IMMEDIATE :var``. |
| `legacy_audit.analyzers.dynsql` | Rebuilding SQL text that code assembles at run time, shared by the C/Pro*C and COBOL analyzers (the Java analyzer keeps its own tree-based version with the same fields). |
| `legacy_audit.analyzers.embedded` | Embedded SQL (``EXEC SQL ... ;`` in Pro*C, ``EXEC SQL ... END-EXEC`` in COBOL / Pro*COBOL). |
| `legacy_audit.analyzers.integrations` | Building ``Integration`` facts. Each usage is recorded per (type, target, direction); MQ/JMS queues per queue, their direction derived from producers and consumers when everything is merged. The merge then keeps one integration per interface (``consolidation_key``). |
| `legacy_audit.analyzers.sqltools` | SQL helpers shared by every analyzer that finds SQL: detection, normalization (for distinct counting), statement type, tables (``sqlglot`` with a regex fallback) and vendor features. |
| `legacy_audit.analyzers.textutil` | Small text and XML helpers shared by analyzers. |
